findings.summary: build_features standardizes using the full dataset's mean/std before the train/test split (called at train.py:15, split at train.py:16), leaking test statistics into training features and making the reported test AUC optimistic.

Scaling parameters are not saved, so at inference build_features scales new data with that batch's own statistics; a single row yields NaN std and all-NaN features, and small batches get a different scale than training (train/serve skew).
Constant (zero-variance) columns give std() of 0, so the division produces NaN or inf and LogisticRegression raises a ValueError.
